$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a}}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}A_{k}z_{k1}y_{k}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(A_{k}y_{k}y_{k}^{\top}+\sum_{j\in S_{a},\;j\neq k}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}A_{k}z_{k1}y_{k}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=0. $$

Hence

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}z_{i1}y_{i}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a}}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}A_{i}z_{i1}y_{i}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle=r_{a}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\sqrt{n}A_{1}z_{11}}{\sigma\left(z_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\cdot y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a}}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle r_{a}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\sqrt{n}z_{11}}{\sigma\left(z_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\cdot y_{1}^{\top}\left(y_{1}^{\top}y_{1}+\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}\mid A_{1}=1,\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]\cdot\mathbb{P}(A_{1}=1) \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\sqrt{n}w_{11}}{\sigma\left(w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}+y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\right)}\cdot y_{1}^{\top}\left(y_{1}^{\top}y_{1}+\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right], \displaystyle\text{where }w_{11}=(z_{11}\mid A_{1}=1) \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\sqrt{n}w_{11}}{\sigma\left(w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}+y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\right)}\cdot\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]\quad\text{(Sherman\textendash Morrison)} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}(1+e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}})\cdot\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}\right]\cdot\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\right] \displaystyle+ \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]\cdot\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]. $$

Similar to Lemma E.3, we can show that the deterministic equivalent of $\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}$ is

$$ \frac{n}{n_{a}}\cdot\frac{2}{1-\frac{2p}{n_{a}}}I_{p-1}=\frac{2n}{n_{a}-2p}I_{p-1}. $$

Since $\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\left\|\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\right\|$ is bounded, by uniform integrability we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\frac{2n}{n_{a}-2p}\|y_{1}\|^{2}}{1+\frac{2n}{n_{a}-2p}\|y_{1}\|^{2}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\frac{2n}{n_{a}-2p}\frac{p}{n}}{1+\frac{2n}{n_{a}-2p}\frac{p}{n}} \displaystyle=2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{p}{n_{a}}=2\kappa_{a}. $$

Further, by Lemma D.3 we know

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}\right]=2e_{\gamma,0}. $$

We then find $\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]$ . Since the first row of the projection matrix $P$ is $\frac{\beta^{\top}}{\|\beta\|}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\tilde{\beta}_{1}}{\sqrt{n}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}(P\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}})_{1}=\frac{\beta^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}}{\sqrt{n}\|\beta\|}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma. $$

Thus

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}w_{11}e^{-\sqrt{n}w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt{n}z_{11}e^{-\sqrt{n}z_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\mid A_{1}=1,\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\sqrt{n}ze^{-\sqrt{n}z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot p(A_{1}=1\mid z_{11}=z)\cdot p\left(z_{11}=z\right)dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\sqrt{n}ze^{-\sqrt{n}z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot\frac{1}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{nz^{2}}{2}}dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot\frac{1}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}e^{-\frac{z^{2}}{2}}dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\right], $$

where the last step is because the limit of the conditional expectation is a constant that does not depend on $\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}$ .

For large $n$ , there exists $c$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\frac{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\right|\leq\left|{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}\right|\leq ze^{-cz}, $$

Thus by dominant convergence theorem

$$ \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\right]=2\mathbb{E}\left[\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{ze^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\right]=2\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{ze^{-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma z}}{1+e^{-\gamma z}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{z-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}{1+e^{-\gamma(z-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma)}}\right]e^{\frac{(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma)^{2}}{2}}=2e^{\frac{(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma)^{2}}{2}}e_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}, $$

where the second last step is obtained via a change of variable.

Next we find

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]. $$

We have shown

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}=2\kappa_{a}\quad\text{a.s.} $$

We then show

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[2\kappa_{a}e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]. $$

We only need to show

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}-2\kappa_{a}\right)\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=0. $$

By Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}-2\kappa_{a}\right)\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}-2\kappa_{a}\right)^{2}\right]\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]}. $$

Note that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-2y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{2\|\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\|^{2}}{n}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{2\|\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\|^{2}}{n}}\right]. $$

Further,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=2}^{p}\tilde{\beta}_{i}^{2}=\frac{1}{n}\|\tilde{\beta}\|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\tilde{\beta}_{1}^{2}=\frac{1}{n}\|\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\frac{\beta^{\top}}{\|\beta\|}\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}})^{2} \displaystyle\xrightarrow{a.s.} \displaystyle\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}+\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}\gamma^{2}-\frac{(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma^{2})^{2}}{\gamma^{2}}=\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}. $$

Thus we have

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{2\|\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\|^{2}}{n}}\right]=e^{2\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}=O(1). $$

Moreover, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}-2\kappa_{a}\right)^{2}\right]=o(1). $$

Thus we have shown

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[2\kappa_{a}e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]. $$

As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{1}}\cdot e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[2\kappa_{a}e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\kappa_{a}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{\|\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}\|^{2}}{2n}}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right]=2\kappa_{a}e^{\frac{1}{2}\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}. $$

Therefore

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}z_{i1}y_{i}\mid\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\cdot 2e_{\gamma,0}\cdot 2\kappa_{a}+\frac{r_{a}}{2}\cdot 2e^{\frac{\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma\right)^{2}}{2}}e_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}\cdot 2\kappa_{a}e^{\frac{1}{2}\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}+o(1) \displaystyle=2\kappa\left(e_{\gamma,0}+e^{\frac{\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma\right)^{2}+\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}{2}}e_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}\right)+o(1), $$

which implies

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}z_{i1}y_{i}\right] \displaystyle=2\kappa\left(e_{\gamma,0}+e^{\frac{\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma\right)^{2}+\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}{2}}e_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}\right)+o(1). $$

We then find the limit of

$$ \frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)\right]. $$

Similar to the previous argument, we can treat $\hat{\beta}_{S_{b}}$ as a deterministic vector. Note that

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}}\right)\right] \displaystyle+ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right)\right]+\kappa. $$

Further, for any $i\neq j,\;i,j\in S_{a}$ , by symmetry of $y_{i}$ we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[A_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\left(\sum_{k\in S_{a}}A_{k}y_{k}y_{k}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{A_{j}y_{j}}e^{-z_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[y_{i}^{\top}\left(y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}+\sum_{k\neq i}A_{k}y_{k}y_{k}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{A_{j}y_{j}}e^{-z_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right]=0. $$

Therefore

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right)\right] \displaystyle=\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[A_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a}}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{A_{i}y_{i}}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle r_{a}\mathbb{E}\left[A_{1}y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\in S_{a}}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{A_{1}y_{1}}e^{-z_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[y_{1}^{\top}\left(y_{1}y_{1}^{\top}+\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{y_{1}}e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\right]\mathbb{E}\left[y_{1}^{\top}\left(y_{1}y_{1}^{\top}+\sum_{j\in S_{a},j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{y_{1}}e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{r_{a}}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\right]\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-y_{1}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\frac{y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{y_{1}}}{1+y_{1}^{\top}\left(\sum_{j\neq 1}A_{j}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\right)^{-1}{y_{1}}}\right]\quad\text{(Sherman\textendash Morrison)}. $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-w_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\right]=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[e^{-z_{11}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\mid A_{1}=1\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-\sqrt{n}z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot p\left(A_{1}=1\mid z_{11}=z\right)\cdot p\left(z_{11}=z\right)dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-\sqrt{n}z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot\frac{1}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|}}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{nz^{2}}{2}}dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}\cdot\frac{1}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}e^{-\frac{z^{2}}{2}}dz \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{e^{-z\tilde{\beta}_{1}/\sqrt{n}}}{1+e^{-z\|\beta\|/\sqrt{n}}}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 2\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{e^{-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma z}}{1+e^{-\gamma z}}\right]=2\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{1+e^{-\gamma(z-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma)}}\right]e^{\frac{(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma)^{2}}{2}}=2e^{\frac{\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma\right)^{2}}{2}}q_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}, $$

We have

$$ \displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\kappa+r_{a}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{e^{-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma z}}{1+e^{-\gamma z}}\right]\cdot 2\kappa_{a}e^{\frac{1}{2}\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}=2\kappa\left(\frac{1}{2}+e^{\frac{\left(\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma\right)^{2}+\kappa_{b}\left(\sigma_{b}^{*}\right)^{2}}{2}}q_{\gamma,-\alpha_{b}^{*}\gamma}\right). $$

We then show

$$ \text{Var}\left(\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}\frac{A_{i}y_{i}}{\sigma\left(z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}\right)}\right)\right)=o(1). $$

We know $\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}}\right)$ converges to some constant. Furthermore, uniform integrability holds for the sequence. Therefore we only need to show

$$ \text{Var}\left(\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}}\right)\right)=o(1). $$

Note that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}e^{-z_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}}}\right) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}A_{i}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i\in S_{a}}{A_{i}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}\cdot e^{-z_{i1}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\right) \displaystyle\sim \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}\cdot e^{-w_{i1}\tilde{\beta}_{1}}\right). $$

For all $i,j\in\{1,2,\ldots,\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor\}$ , define

$$ l_{i}=e^{-w_{i1}\tilde{\beta}_{1}},\quad T=\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right), $$

$$ T^{(l_{j})}=\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left({y_{j}e^{y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{j}^{{}^{\prime}}+\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right), $$

$$ T^{(y_{j})}=\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right). $$

Since $y_{1},y_{2},\ldots,y_{n_{a}},l_{1},l_{2},\ldots,l_{n_{a}}$ are independent, by Efron–Stein inequality, we have

$$ \displaystyle\operatorname{Var}(T)\leq\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}\left(T-T^{(l_{i})}\right)^{2}+\sum_{j=1}^{\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}\left(T-T^{(y_{j})}\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle=O(n)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{(l_{1})}\right)^{2}\right]+O(n)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{(y_{1})}\right)^{2}\right]. $$

Define $\tilde{n}_{a}=\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor.$ Then

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{(l_{1})}\right)^{2}\right]=\frac{1}{n^{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}e^{y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\right)^{2}\cdot\left(l_{j}-l_{j}^{{}^{\prime}}\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{n^{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{2}e^{2y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\cdot\left(l_{j}-l_{j}^{{}^{\prime}}\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{1}{n^{2}}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]\cdot\mathbb{E}\left[e^{4y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}\cdot\left(l_{j}-l_{j}^{\prime}\right)^{4}\right]} \displaystyle= \displaystyle O\left(\frac{1}{n^{2}}\right)\sqrt{\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]}. $$

Thus in order to show

$$ O(n)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{\left(l_{1}\right)}\right)^{2}\right]=o(1), $$

we only need to show

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]=o(n^{2}). $$

By Sherman–Morrison formula, we have

$$ \displaystyle\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}=\frac{\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\leq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}}{1+y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\leq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}} \displaystyle=O(1)\cdot\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}. $$

Thus we only need to show

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]=o(n^{2}). $$

In fact, we only need to show

$$ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}=o(1)\quad\text{a.s.} $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}_{a}}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j} \displaystyle=y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}+\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}, $$

and

$$ y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}=O(1)\quad\text{a.s.}, $$

we only need to show

$$ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}=o(1)\quad\text{a.s.} $$

By symmetry the expectation of the left hand side is 0. Hence we only need to show

$$ \frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{2}\right]=o(1). $$

We have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-2}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\tilde{n}_{a},i\neq j}y_{i}\right)\right]=O(1). $$

Thus we have proved

$$ O(n)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{\left(l_{1}\right)}\right)^{2}\right]=o(1). $$

Next we show

$$ O(n)\mathbb{E}\left[\left(T-T^{\left(y_{1}\right)}\right)^{2}\right]=o(1). $$

Note that

$$ \displaystyle T-T^{\left(y_{1}\right)} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)+\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}e^{y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{j} \displaystyle+ \displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}-\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\right] \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right). $$

Thus we only need to show

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{n}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right]=o(n^{-1}), \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}-\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\right]\right.\right. \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\left.\left.\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right]=o(n^{-1}). $$

First we show

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right]=o\left(1\right). $$

Since

$$ \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(y_{i}e^{y_{j}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{j}\right)=o(1)\quad\text{a.s.}, $$

we only need to show

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right]=o(1). $$

By Sherman–Morrison,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right) \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\frac{1}{y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}}. $$

Thus

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle C\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right)^{2}\right]+o(1) \displaystyle\text{ for some constant }C \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{C}{n^{2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-2}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\right] \displaystyle+ \displaystyle o(1)=o(1). $$

Finally we show

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\Big)^{\top}\Big[\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\Big)^{-1}-\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\Big)^{-1}\Big] \displaystyle\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\Big)\Big)^{2}\Big]=o(1). $$

Note that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}-\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\right] \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right) \displaystyle= \displaystyle-\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left[\frac{\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}}{1+y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}}\right] \displaystyle\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\right) \displaystyle= \displaystyle C\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j} \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}^{\top}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}+o(1)\quad\text{ for some constant }C. $$

Since

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right]=0, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right]^{2}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}y_{j}^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\right. \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\left.\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{n^{1.5}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-2}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)\right]=o(1), $$

we know

$$ \frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}=o(1)\quad\text{a.s.}, $$

which implies

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]=o(1). $$

Similarly we can show

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt[4]{n}}\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}^{\top}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}l_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\left\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\right\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}y_{j}\right)^{4}\right]=o(1). $$

By Cauchy-Schwarz, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\Big[\Big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}\Big)^{\top}\Big[\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\Big)^{-1}-\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}y_{i}y_{i}^{\top}\Big)^{-1}\Big] \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\Big(\sum_{1\leq i\leq\lfloor\frac{n_{a}}{2}\rfloor,i\neq j}{y_{i}e^{y_{i}^{\top}\tilde{\beta}_{2:p}}}l_{i}\Big)\Big)^{2}\Big]=o(1). $$

This completes the proof.

## F Proofs of Intermediate Results

### F.1 Proof of Lemma C.1

Define

$$ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}x_{i}^{\top},\quad V=\frac{1}{n}\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}\right)\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}^{\top}\right). $$

Then

$$ \displaystyle a^{\top}(O-Q)b=a^{\top}(U-V)^{-1}b-a^{\top}U^{-1}b \displaystyle= \displaystyle a^{\top}\left[U^{-1}+\frac{1}{1-\text{Tr}(VU^{-1})}U^{-1}VU^{-1}\right]b-a^{\top}U^{-1}b=\frac{1}{1-\text{Tr}(VU^{-1})}a^{\top}U^{-1}VU^{-1}b, $$

where the second equality is due to the lemma in [78], which also implies that the denominator is non-zero.

We know

$$ \displaystyle\text{Tr}(VU^{-1})=\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}\right)^{-1}\cdot\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}\right)^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}x_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}\right), $$

and

$$ \displaystyle a^{\top}U^{-1}VU^{-1}b \displaystyle= \displaystyle\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}\right)^{-1}\left[a^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}x_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}\right)\right] \displaystyle\cdot \displaystyle\left[b^{\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}x_{i}^{\top}\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_{i}x_{i}\right)\right]. $$

Thus

## G Proof of Theorem 3.4

In this section, we first state the full result of Theorem 3.4. To this end, we need some additional notation.

Fix any ridge penalty parameter $\lambda>0$ . For any $i=1,2,3$ , let $\left(\alpha_{i}^{(\lambda)},\sigma_{i}^{(\lambda)},\lambda_{i}^{(\lambda)}\right)$ be the solution to the system of equations (4.12) in [107], where the covariates are of dimension $n_{i}\times p$ with i.i.d. entries $\sim\mathcal{N}\left(0,\frac{1}{n_{i}}\right)$ , the signal strength is $\gamma^{2}$ , and the ridge penalty parameter is $\lambda$ . Moreover, define

$$ \tilde{\alpha}_{i}^{(\lambda)}=\alpha_{i}^{(\lambda)}\cdot\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{\left(\lambda\right)}}{\kappa_{a}},\quad\tilde{\sigma}_{i}^{(\lambda)}=\sigma_{i}^{(\lambda)}\cdot\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{\left(\lambda\right)}}{\kappa_{a}},\quad\tilde{\lambda}_{i}^{(\lambda)}=\lambda_{i}^{(\lambda)}. $$

Then the asymptotic variance $\left(\sigma_{cf}^{(\lambda)}\right)^{2}$ in Theorem 3.4 is the same as the expression for $\sigma_{cf}^{2}$ in Theorem 3.3, except that $(\alpha_{i}^{*},\sigma_{i}^{*},\lambda_{i}^{*})$ is replaced by $\left(\tilde{\alpha}_{i}^{(\lambda/r_{i})},\tilde{\sigma}_{i}^{(\lambda/r_{i})},\tilde{\lambda}_{i}^{(\lambda/r_{i})}\right)\;\;\forall i\in\{1,2,3\}$ .

The proof of Theorem 3.4 can be obtained by modifying the proof of Theorem 3.3. In particular, we only need to modify the lemmas involved in the proof of Theorem 3.3 that use properties of MLE for logistic regression models.

#### Lemma G.1.

Fix any ridge penalty parameter $\lambda>0$ . Fix any $(a,b,c)$ , a permutation of $(1,2,3)$ . Assume the setting described in section 2. Let $x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ be any sample in $S_{c}$ . Then the random vector $\left(\begin{array}[]{c}x^{\top}\beta\\ x^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\end{array}\right)$ converges in distribution to a multivariate normal distribution with mean zero and variance $\Sigma$ , where

$$ \Sigma=\begin{bmatrix}\gamma^{2}&\tilde{\alpha}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\gamma^{2}\\
\tilde{\alpha}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\gamma^{2}&\quad\kappa_{a}\left(\tilde{\sigma}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\tilde{\alpha}_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}\right)^{2}\gamma^{2}\end{bmatrix}. $$

Conditioned on $S_{a},S_{b}$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}x^{\top}\beta\\
x^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\end{array}\right)\sim N\left(\mathbf{0},\frac{1}{n}\begin{bmatrix}\|\beta\|^{2}&\beta^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\\
\beta^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}&\|\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\|^{2}\end{bmatrix}\right). $$

By assumption

$$ \frac{\|\beta\|^{2}}{n}\rightarrow\gamma^{2}. $$

Note that $\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}$ is estimated from $S_{a}$ , where $X_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{a}\times p}$ with i.i.d. entries $\sim N(0,\frac{1}{n})$ . Define

$$ \beta^{{}^{\prime}}=\sqrt{r_{a}}\beta,\quad\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{{}^{\prime}}=\sqrt{r_{a}}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)},\quad X_{a}^{{}^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{r_{a}}}X_{a} $$

Then $X_{a}^{{}^{\prime}}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{a}\times p}$ with i.i.d. entries $\sim N(0,\frac{1}{n_{a}})$ , and $X_{a}\beta=X_{a}^{{}^{\prime}}\beta^{{}^{\prime}},X_{a}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}=X_{a}^{{}^{\prime}}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{{}^{\prime}}$ . Moreover,

$$ \frac{\|\beta^{{}^{\prime}}\|^{2}}{n_{a}}=\frac{r_{a}\|\beta\|^{2}}{n_{a}}=\frac{\|\beta\|^{2}}{n}\rightarrow\gamma^{2}. $$

According to Chapter 4, Result 1 in [107],

$$ \frac{1}{p}(\beta^{{}^{\prime}})^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{{}^{\prime}}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\frac{\alpha_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}}{p}\left(\beta^{\prime}\right)^{\top}\beta^{\prime}\cdot\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}}{\kappa_{a}}. $$

This implies

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\beta^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}=\alpha_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}\gamma^{2}\cdot\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}}{\kappa_{a}}\quad\text{almost surely.} $$

Moreover, applying Chapter 4, Result 1 in [107] with $\psi(t,u)=t^{2}$ yields

$$ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\|\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{{}^{\prime}}\|^{2}}{p}=\left[(\sigma_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})})^{2}+(\alpha_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})})^{2}\frac{r_{a}\gamma^{2}}{\kappa}\right]\cdot\left(\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{\left(\lambda/r_{a}\right)}}{\kappa_{a}}\right)^{2}\quad\text{almost surely.} $$

Thus

$$ \frac{\|\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\|^{2}}{n}=\frac{\|\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{\prime}\|^{2}}{p}\cdot\frac{p}{n}\cdot\frac{1}{r_{a}}\xrightarrow{a.s.}\left[\kappa_{a}(\sigma_{a}^{\left(\lambda/r_{a}\right)})^{2}+(\alpha_{a}^{\left(\lambda/r_{a}\right)})^{2}\gamma^{2}\right]\cdot\left(\frac{\kappa_{a}-\lambda\lambda_{a}^{\left(\lambda/r_{a}\right)}}{\kappa_{a}}\right)^{2}. $$

Hence we know

$$ \displaystyle\left(\begin{array}[]{c}x^{\top}\beta\\
x^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\end{array}\right)\xrightarrow{d}N\left(\mathbf{0},\begin{bmatrix}\gamma^{2}&\tilde{\alpha}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\gamma^{2}\\
\tilde{\alpha}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\gamma^{2}&\quad\kappa_{a}\left(\tilde{\sigma}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}_{a}\right)^{2}+\left(\tilde{\alpha}_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}\right)^{2}\gamma^{2}\end{bmatrix}\right), $$

which does not depend on $S_{a},S_{b}$ . This completes the proof of the lemma. ∎

Below we state the properties of MLE for logistic regression models that are used in the proof of Theorem 3.3, and show how they can be modified to prove Theorem 3.4.

(i) The proof of Lemma B.3 and C.6 uses the following property:

$$ \frac{1}{n}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{T}\hat{\beta}_{S_{c}}=\alpha_{a}^{*}\alpha_{c}^{*}\gamma^{2}+o(1)\quad\text{a.s.}\quad\forall a,c\in\{1,2,3\}. $$

Similar to the proof of Lemma G.1, with an extension of Chapter 4, Result 1 in [107], we can show

$$ \frac{1}{n}\left(\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\right)^{T}\hat{\beta}_{S_{c}}^{(\lambda)}=\tilde{\alpha}_{a}^{(\lambda/r_{a})}\tilde{\alpha}_{c}^{(\lambda/r_{c})}\gamma^{2}+o(1)\quad\text{a.s.}\quad\forall a,c\in\{1,2,3\}. $$

(ii) The proof of Lemma C.6 and C.8 uses Lemma 21 in [107]. Since the ridge penalty is strongly convex, its Hessian is positive. Thus Lemma 16 in [107] still holds if we replace the negative log-likelihood with the sum of the negative log-likelihood and the ridge penalty. The remaining proof for Lemma 21 in [107] also holds, which implies that Lemma 21 in [107] also applies to ridge regularized estimates.

(iii) Lemma D.6 characterizes the asymptotic distribution of $\left(\begin{array}[]{c}x^{\top}\beta\\ x^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}\end{array}\right),$ where $x\in\mathbb{R}^{p}$ is any sample in $S_{c}$ , and $(a,b,c)$ is any permutation of $(1,2,3)$ . Correspondingly, Lemma G.1 characterizes the asymptotic distribution of $\left(\begin{array}[]{c}x^{\top}\beta\\ x^{\top}\hat{\beta}_{S_{a}}^{(\lambda)}\end{array}\right)$ .

After modifying the lemmas mentioned above, we can prove Theorem 3.4 in a similar fashion as the proof of Theorem 3.3.
